decision: Reject short-string ASCII precheck bypass; production encoder restored exactly.
experiment: Use the general escaped UTF8 loop directly for strings shorter than 32 UTF16 units; retain native ASCII precheck for longer strings. No allocation or memory policy changes.
findings: Profile assigns 23.88% sampled self time to cursor advancement and own-key generator, 10.16% to ASCII precheck; inlining and sampling limit attribution.

Row-array median improvement varies from 9.1% to 1.0%; small-row median worsens in both comparisons. Expanded cases show 16% overhead for eight-character ASCII and 8.9% for 31-character ASCII. No durable aggregate improvement established.

Expanded benchmark checks actual JSON bytes and zero budget charges for 1/8/31/32/33/256/4096-character ASCII, Unicode, escaped quotes and lone surrogates, plus mixed structures and 20000-level nesting.
validation: Candidate JSON encoding/size/standard semantics suites passed; production code restored and rebuilt. No whole-runtime or cloud-throughput inference.
next: Investigate cursor/generator overhead with a generic admitted traversal contract; retain depth safety and exact-byte oracle. Avoid another frame reset/pooling experiment without new evidence.
